When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **2**/**10**, watch level vs VIX Spike Tier **2**/**4**, **60%** probability, backwardation and skew active
Price is calm but options buyers pay up for protection and the VIX curve is inverted. Trust the options market for timing a volatility pop, and trust the Crash Index for the lack of damage so far, because no confluence has confirmed.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime State **33**, stable, no regime shift vs Divergence composite ELEVATED with **51.2%** of **43** pairs diverging
The regime score reacts to levels while divergence tracks how relationships are changing. Trust the divergence reading as the early warning, since correlations usually break before the regime score moves.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **56**, accumulate vs Net divergence bias **14** with **18** bearish pairs against **4** bullish
Dip buying says sentiment is washed out enough to start nibbling, yet the internals lean bearish by a wide margin. Trust the internals for sizing and treat the contrarian signal as permission for small starter positions only.
Today's tension
Price action is calm while options and cross-asset correlations flag stress underneath.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at only **2** of **10**, the regime score reads stable at **33**, and no confluence is active. The contrarian gauge at **56** says dip buyers have a partial green light.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector sits at Tier **2** of **4** with a **60%** probability, backwardation and skew are both on, and **51.2%** of tracked pairs are diverging. The Nasdaq 100 is down **3.5%** over five days while the Dow is up **1.6%**.
The tell: Whether VIX backwardation spreads to credit (HYG), small caps (B2) or the yen (JPY). Any one of those turning on means the stress has left the options market and reached real money.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The call is cautious but not defensive. Nothing has broken, yet little is confirmed healthy either. The Crash Index reads 2 of 10, the regime state is stable at 33, and the macro regime is TRANSITIONAL at only 25% confidence. That low confidence tells you the market has not decided what it is.

The tension sits in the options market. The VIX Spike Detector is at Tier 2 of 4 with a 60% probability, and both backwardation and skew are active. Backwardation means near term fear costs more than far term fear, which is what traders pay for when they expect a move soon. Add the Nasdaq 100 at -3.5% over five days against the Dow at +1.6%, and you see money rotating out of growth rather than leaving equities altogether.

For positioning, the contrarian score of 56 supports small starter buys, and the internals say keep them small. Hold dry powder for a better entry and avoid adding to the weakest growth exposure. The main risk is the 18 bearish pairs against 4 bullish in the divergence read. The stance flips bearish if any of the three T1 confluences (credit, small caps, yen) turns on. It flips constructive if backwardation fades while the Nasdaq 100 stops falling.

AI read · macro regime

The regime state score of 33 is stable with a MIXED bias, so the signals compete. The Dow at +1.6% against the Nasdaq 100 at -3.5% supports the rotation story.

Position for that with balance. Keep core holdings, avoid concentrated growth bets, and build any contrarian buys slowly given the 56 accumulate reading.

Confidence of only 25% means you should size smaller than usual until it climbs. A rise in that confidence number, especially toward a defensive or contraction label, is the cue to commit to a direction.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two things that usually move together have started moving apart. Correlation drift is the measured change in how tightly they move together, shown as a before and after number.

Right now the composite zone is ELEVATED, with 51.2% of 43 pairs diverging, a net bias of 14, and 18 bearish pairs against 4 bullish. The mother jaws score is 100.

The six top pairs all score 80. Stocks and bonds flipped from a correlation of +0.69 to -0.36, which means bonds are no longer moving with stocks the way they did.

Regional banks against financials went from +0.29 to -0.72, a sign that bank stress is separating from the broad sector. High beta against low volatility stocks fell from +0.94 to +0.40, so risk appetite is splitting.

Visa against Mastercard dropped from +0.83 to -0.66, which is an unusual break between two near twins. Many relationships are changing at once, and that tends to come before a regime change.

It does not set the timing, so use it to trim risk where several of these pairs point the same way.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

No confluence is active today. T1 is live through VIX backwardation, but its three partners are quiet: credit stress (HYG), small cap drawdown (B2) and yen safe haven flow (JPY).

That means the fear stays inside the options market. Credit has not widened, small caps are not breaking down, and money is not running to the yen.

You should not lean defensive on this alone. A single signal is a heads up, and conviction needs a partner.

The cleanest warning would be T1 with HYG, because credit is where real stress shows first. Keep the three conditions on your screen and act only when one turns on.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is rotating away from growth and Asia is the weak link. South Korea's KOSPI (^KS11) leads the laggards at -6.0% over five days, a sharp drop that points to pressure in the tech and chip supply chain.

Australia (^AXJO) is flat at +0.3%. In Europe the Swiss market (^SSMI) leads at +3.5%, a defensive heavy index, while the Euro Stoxx 50 (^STOXX50E) slips -0.9%.

In the US the Dow (^DJI) at +1.6% leads and the Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) at -3.5% lags. Crypto is quiet, with Solana at +1.3% and Ether at +0.5%, so there is no panic bid or flight there.

For the US session, expect pressure on tech and chip stocks to continue, with steadier trade in defensives and old economy sectors. A Korean rebound would be the first sign that the growth selloff is easing.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 2/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges disagree, and the disagreement is coherent. The Crash Index at 2 of 10 measures damage already done in price, and there is little of it.

The VIX Spike Detector at Tier 2 of 4, with a 60% probability, measures what options traders expect next. Skew is active, so downside puts cost more than upside calls.

Backwardation is active, so the front of the VIX curve is priced above the back. Together they describe a market that looks calm on the screen while buyers pay up for insurance.

Trust the options market on timing, because it prices the future while the Crash Index only counts the past. Tier 2 is a middle reading, which keeps this a warning and short of an alarm.

The reading that escalates the call is a Crash Index rise to 4 or more while backwardation persists. The reading that relaxes it is backwardation flattening with the Crash Index still at 2.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 2/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
